runners_data.name: South Dakota
runners_data.note: A P O'Brien hold-up filly with a consistent form string of placed efforts on Good going — her 4/4 record on similar ground is her biggest asset, and this strong pace is exactly the scenario she needs to arrive late with purpose over a suitable 7½f trip.
runners_data.comment: Never far away in recent starts, South Dakota brings solid each-way claims having run over today's trip and going, and 28 days between runs leaves him fresh; the concern is that he remains winless in his last four, suggesting he may find one too good again.

runners_data.name: Full Volume
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on Good and finished second in the same company for Harrington — Shane Foley takes over from the saddle and she has legitimate front-running claims, though sustaining the lead under pressure in a four-way speed duel is the key concern; headgear not reported.
runners_data.comment: A winner three starts back, Full Volume has since been held to sixth on his latest outing, and the 132 lb he carries from stall one is a notable ask; experience over today's trip and going offers some encouragement, but our rating suggests he faces a stiff task against stronger company here.

runners_data.name: Joga Bonito
runners_data.note: Won last time at 7f on Soft for Twomey, and the switch back to Good ground (2 from 4 on similar) introduces a small question mark, but recent winning form gives confidence; she will try to lead and her finishing record suggests she may get first run on tired rivals if she can settle in front.
runners_data.comment: Joga Bonito arrives on the back of a win last time out and has experience of today's trip and conditions, making him a genuine threat from stall two off 130 lb; the weight he shoulders is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Lars Soldier
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a busy campaign (13 days since last run) who has placed five times from seven starts on Good — Wesley Joyce (3lb claim) is an asset in a 2yo handicap and he should be finding a comfortable pitch just off the front-running battle.
runners_data.comment: Lars Soldier ran a solid second one start back and has experience of both today's trip and going, while his rating of 93 suggests he holds strong claims here; the fifth last time out is the one to look past.

runners_data.name: Ruler's Control
runners_data.note: Won over 5f on Heavy for Joseph O'Brien but has failed to fire at 6f and 7f on Good since, suggesting the trip extension and surface combination may not be ideal — he will likely try to lead but has no form to suggest he can sustain it at this level over 7½f; tongue tie noted.
runners_data.comment: Ruler's Control landed a win three starts back and has run over today's trip and going, giving him solid claims from stall seven off 130 lb; a couple of below-par efforts since are the only reservation, but he appeals as the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Cudawudashuda
runners_data.note: Lightly raced (one run, finished 6th over 8f on Good) with an OR of 120 that reflects the handicapper's assessment on very little evidence — Colin Keane's booking is the primary reason to take seriously and the strong pace could suit a horse arriving late, but he remains an unknown quantity.
runners_data.comment: Cudawudashuda is yet to score in recent starts, and 59 days between runs is a notable fitness query, though he has run over today's trip and going before and carries a straightforward 126 lb from stall nine.

runners_data.name: Panhandle
runners_data.note: Two starts, two finishes in double figures on Good ground, and tagged as fading in the finish — Gary Carroll will try to find the lead but the evidence suggests this horse has been sent off at big prices for good reason and is unlikely to sustain competitive involvement past the halfway stage.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last two starts and ranked bottom of nine on our figures, Panhandle faces a stiff ask here, though he has run over today's going before and returns on a quick eight-day turnaround suggesting connections are keen.

runners_data.name: The Long Haul
runners_data.note: Two outings yielding a 5th and 12th, both on Good going, represent thin form at this level — James Ryan takes a prominent pitch, but a horse returning on limited evidence and without any placed effort offers little encouragement even in a race where the pace may open things up.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last two starts and ranked eighth of nine on our figures, The Long Haul faces a stiff ask here, though he has run over today's going before and a 15-day turnaround suggests he arrives fresh enough.

runners_data.name: Wunderschon
runners_data.note: One run (7th over 7f on Good) for Harrington, who also saddles Full Volume — Keithen Kennedy (5lb claim) is an inexperienced combination with a deeply unexposed runner, and while the trip is not new, there is simply too little information to project with confidence; lightly raced flag applies.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last start and ranked seventh of nine on our figures, Wunderschon faces a stiff task here, though she has run over today's trip before and returns after a 34-day break with freshness potentially on her side.

races.paceDynamic: Panhandle, Full Volume, and Joga Bonito are all confirmed front-runners who will immediately contest the early lead over Roscommon's 7½f, creating a genuinely contested gallop from the off — Ruler's Control adds a fourth pace presence, ensuring no one gets a soft lead or dictates from a crawl. This multi-horse battle for the front over the first two furlongs will burn energy among those leadres, stretching the field and ensuring the pace is unrelenting rather than tactical; at 7½f on Good turf, that is enough to put genuine stamina under the microscope. Lars Soldier and The Long Haul are likely to sit just behind the friction point, with South Dakota and the unknown quantities Cudawudashuda and Wunderschon tracking from midfield or off the pace. The race shape strongly favours hold-up and late-finishing profiles — horses who can switch off in the early chaos, conserve energy, and produce a sustained run in the final two furlongs will be best served by what this contested pace creates.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the four-way pace battle burns out the leaders before the turn, releasing the late-runners into a clear advantage.
scenarios.body: Full Volume, Joga Bonito, and Ruler's Control gut each other setting a fierce gallop, leaving them spent in the straight as South Dakota and Cudawudashuda sweep through on fresh legs. At 7½f, the distance is long enough for hold-up types to mow down a field that has over-exerted itself in the opening half of the race.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Leader Clears Early
scenarios.trigger: If one of the front-runners — most likely Full Volume or Joga Bonito — gets a split-second jump and dictates at a controlled pace while rivals cancel each other out.
scenarios.body: Full Volume, who won over this distance and goes on Good, or Joga Bonito, who has the strongest recent form having won last time, could slip into a rhythm on the front end if the others tangle in a speed duel. A horse sitting a length or two off the early pace leader at a comfortable clip, such as Lars Soldier, could also benefit from any brief lull.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Sits Perfect
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is fierce but not suicidal, and a horse just off the leaders tracks through into a winning position without exhausting itself in early traffic.
scenarios.body: Lars Soldier or The Long Haul, sitting just behind the early duel in a prominent position, could inherit the race if the lead horses run each other into the ground at a pace that is fast but not extreme. A prominent runner who avoids the worst of the early battle and hits the straight in the first two has a clear positional advantage.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Defies Logic
scenarios.trigger: If the pace implodes spectacularly early and one of the lightly-raced unknowns, Cudawudashuda or Wunderschon, produces a career-best from the back.
scenarios.body: Colin Keane on Cudawudashuda (OR=120, only one run) is well-placed by the handicapper on a single outing and could be ahead of his mark, swooping late if the field ties itself up. Wunderschon, similarly unexposed, represents a second unknown quantity for trainer Harrington who also saddles Full Volume, though both remain deeply speculative on limited evidence.

watchPoints.text: Watch the opening two furlongs closely — if Panhandle, Full Volume, Joga Bonito, and Ruler's Control all commit to leading, the resulting friction will almost certainly produce a falsely fast early pace that decimates their finishing reserves, making the pace collapse in Scenario A the single most dangerous development in this race.

Full Volume (Shane Foley) and Joga Bonito (W J Lee) are the two front-runners with genuine recent form — if either manages to soften the early pace by out-smarting the others in the first furlong and settling into a rhythm, they become significantly more dangerous than the contested-pace scenario suggests.

South Dakota's hold-up style suits this race shape perfectly but Wayne Lordan will need to find daylight late from the back of a nine-runner field — any traffic trouble at Roscommon's turning straight could cost her the run she needs.

Colin Keane's booking on Cudawudashuda stands out for a horse with one run and an OR of 120 — Keane rarely accepts rides without purpose and connections may know significantly more about this horse's ability than the bare form reveals.

Panhandle's "fades in finish" tag combined with OR=120 and back-to-back last-place finishes suggests this horse is carrying a weight-for-age OR rather than a competitive mark — monitor in the market to see if any significant money confirms otherwise or if this is simply a make-weight pace influence.

races.name: Elphin Handicap

runners_data.name: Givehertilxmas
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse trained by Gerard Keane whose best sim-going performance came over 7f on Good; Colin Keane takes the ride which is a significant booking for a 60-rated mare, but 62 days off the track is a flag and she fades in the finish under pressure.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, though her third last time out shows she can hit the frame; the 62-day absence and a stiff 142 lb are the main negatives, but she has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Phoenix Pairc
runners_data.note: Held up in rear by W J Lee, has run 12 times on Good-style ground with some placed efforts and returns quickly on 11 days' rest; the Roscommon 7f trip suits his profile but the form string shows plenty of 0s and he is yet to win from hold-up.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Phoenix Pairc faces a stiff ask from stall 17 carrying 142 lb, and her recent string of sevenths and unplaced efforts offers little encouragement, though she has run over today's trip and going and returns on a quick turnaround of 11 days.

runners_data.name: Angel Of Promise
runners_data.note: Ben Coen rides this hold-up filly for Edward Lynam who has just one runner in the 14-day window; she fades in the finish and the step back up to 7½f from recent 6f runs is untested territory, with 50 days off adding uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts, Angel Of Promise nonetheless catches the eye on fitness grounds returning after 50 days, with experience of today's distance and going working in her favour; drawn 18, she carries 139 lb and our rating of 60 marks her out as one to include.

runners_data.name: Shamanka
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type partnered by claimer Jack Cleary at 5lbs; the 5f form she showed when fourth at Gowran suggests speed is not her primary weapon over this extra distance, though she returns on a quick turnaround in good heart.
runners_data.comment: Shamanka arrives fresh enough on an 11-day turnaround and has run over today's trip and going, though she remains winless in her last five starts — her best recent effort was a fourth three starts back — and carrying 139 lb from stall 13 makes life no easier for a filly rated 57.

runners_data.name: Brains
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner; at ten years old and OR 55 he is reliable in his role but Sam Coen's claim is noted, and the STYLE_FIT flag of 0.94 reflects that any disruption to his lead position would compromise his chance significantly — his value lies entirely in getting a clean break and dictating.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, though Brains did post a second six starts back and returns quickly on 11 days' rest with distance and going experience in his favour; a mark of 55 and 137 lb from stall 14 are the offsetting concerns.

runners_data.name: Cisterna
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery trains and rides this 3-year-old who has a win from 8f on Good ground; with 11 wins and 15 runs on Good and a solid recent form string including a win, he is one of the most reliable Good-ground performers in the field and tends to travel midfield before finishing well.
runners_data.comment: Cisterna has run over today's trip and going, and a win five starts back shows he can find the line, though three consecutive finishes outside the top five in recent starts — including eighth last time out — suggest he faces a stiff ask from 135 lb off stall eight.

runners_data.name: James Henry
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse who the pace map has shifted to midfield because the rear is overcrowded; the 7-year-old carries the STYLE_FIT flag and his recent form shows a run of 0s, with Julian Pietropaolo's 7lb claim offering minimal consolation against more in-form rivals.
runners_data.comment: Ranked top of the field on our rating, James Henry has run over today's trip and going before and, carrying 134 lb from stall nine, returns after a sharp 17-day break with conditions in his favour; the risk is that he has been winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Glen Breeze
runners_data.note: Strong Good-ground form includes a win from 6f and placed efforts, and the horse carries natural prominent inclinations though pushed into a midfield slot by field congestion; Patrick Magee's yard has had no recent winners in the 14-day window, but J M Sheridan's tactical ride could allow Glen Breeze to push closer than the map suggests.
runners_data.comment: Glen Breeze is hard to fancy ranked 14 of 18 on our figures, and his recent form — fifth and sixth in his last two starts — does little to encourage, though he has run over today's trip and going before and arrives with a fair break of 26 days since his last outing.

runners_data.name: Whatswrongnow
runners_data.note: One of only two secondary prominent types with a realistic chance of sitting behind Brains; Adam Browne-Souza's 7lb claim helps the handicapper's rating but the horse's best efforts have come over 5-6f and the step to 7½f on Good is a genuine trip concern.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked 15th of 18 on our figures, Whatswrongnow faces a stiff task here; the second last time out offers a crumb of hope, and he has run over today's trip and going before, but 132 lb from stall 16 adds to the burden.

runners_data.name: Oitentinha
runners_data.note: A 73-day absence is a serious concern for this 4-year-old, and she fades in the finish; her true style is hold-up but field numbers have pushed her into midfield on the map, and her sim-going record of just four runs from six on similar ground is thin evidence.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, including three consecutive ninth-place finishes, Oitentinha faces a stiff ask, though she has run over today's distance and going before and our rating of 55 suggests some latent ability; 73 days off and stall two are the neutral factors to weigh.

runners_data.name: Queen Of Newark
runners_data.note: Returns after 62 days for Matthew J Smith; she fades in the finish and the form figures of 0-0300 with only one placed run in eight similar-going efforts make her one of the least convincing runners at this distance and pace shape, redistribution aside.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked near the foot of our figures, Queen Of Newark is hard to fancy, though she has run over today's distance and going before and the third two starts back offers a rare crumb of encouragement after 62 days off.

runners_data.name: Tamazu
runners_data.note: Coming back from 361 days off, which is the longest absence in the field and demands a large leap of faith; a 7-year-old whose sim-going record shows just five runs from 15 on Good, and the STYLE_FIT flag underlines that sitting in a midfield slot is not his natural home.
runners_data.comment: Tamazu has run over today's trip and going, carries a workable 128 lb from stall three, and a rating of 60 suggests he holds more ability than his official mark implies — yet winless in his last four starts, and 361 days off the track is the significant concern.

runners_data.name: Sunday Sovereign
runners_data.note: A prominent-type who has the pace to press Brains if she gets a clean break; however, she fades in the finish, is 87 days off the track, and the 9-year-old's sim-going record of 12 from 15 on Good shows consistency rather than the finishing kick needed from the front.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 13 of 18 on our figures, Sunday Sovereign faces a stiff task, with an 87-day absence adding further doubt; a third three starts back offers a faint crumb of comfort, and he does have experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: La Campanella
runners_data.note: Has been running in 8-10f company mostly, making this 7½f look shorter than ideal on paper; headgear noted (visor) and returns on just 6 days' rest, though the redistribution to midfield masks a horse whose best efforts have come when given time to settle.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked 16 of 18 on our figures, La Campanella faces a stiff task here, though she has run over today's distance and going before and returns on a quick six-day turnaround showing connections retain some faith.

runners_data.name: Bullet Bourbon
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on Standard for T G McCourt and returns on 16 days; the sim-going record of eight runs on Good without a win there raises a flag, and while he is a 3-year-old with upside, Good-ground form has not matched his All-Weather profile.
runners_data.comment: Bullet Bourbon won one start back but has struggled to build on that, finishing sixth most recently, and her overall consistency in recent starts is mixed. Has run over today's trip and going, carries 122 lb from stall one, and the 16-day turnaround suggests she arrives fit.

runners_data.name: Gordon Bennett
runners_data.note: Peter Fahey sends this 8-year-old out 8 days after his last run with no jockey listed, a notable absence of information; his true character is hold-up and the STYLE_FIT flag of 0.90 is the lowest in the field, meaning the gap between where he will race and where he needs to be is the widest.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Gordon Bennett nonetheless rates well clear of his official mark on our figures, and eight days between runs leaves him fresh enough to strike; the risk is that his recent form has been ragged, with only a third to his name in that spell.

runners_data.name: Draiocht
runners_data.note: Six days between runs for T J O'Mara's 6-year-old who showed a promising third in a 7f Good race recently; his redistribution into midfield papers over a hold-up style, but the Roscommon track's flat profile at least means he won't be undone by undulation if he can find a clear passage.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked last on our figures, Draiocht faces a stiff ask here, though he has run over today's distance and going before and a third two starts back offers a rare glimmer; fresh enough at six days since his last run, the 124 lb burden does him no favours.

runners_data.name: Distillate
runners_data.note: Has natural prominent tendencies and a recent placed effort from 7f on Standard; Adrian McGuinness has had three winners from 21 runners in the 14-day window which is reasonable form, and with Good-ground form rated as just five from 15 runs, the question is whether he can reproduce that standard-surface ability on turf.
runners_data.comment: Distillate was brought down last time out, which clouds her recent form, though a second five starts back shows she can compete at this level; winless in her last five starts and carrying 135 lb from stall 12, she faces a stiff ask here.

races.paceDynamic: Brains is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 18-runner field and, crucially, faces no direct rival likely to press hard for the lead from the outset, meaning a genuinely sustainable gallop is the probable outcome over Roscommon's flat 7½f. With only Whatswrongnow and Sunday Sovereign as secondary prominent types, Brains can dictate comfortably at a tempo that keeps the field strung out without burning off early reserves. The going is a consistent Good throughout the card, favouring horses that travel economically and have the cruising speed to close ground through the final two furlongs rather than those needing an extreme burn-up to set up a late swoop. This race shape therefore most benefits prominent-to-midfield runners with proven Good-ground form who can sit just behind a single uncontested leader and strike from a position of control — pure hold-up horses at the back will be disadvantaged by the modest gallop. A large number of runners listed in midfield are genuine hold-up types — Glen Breeze, Gordon Bennett, Distillate, James Henry, and several others — who have been redistributed forward on the map only because the field carries too many closers to all find their natural position; of those, Glen Breeze and Distillate are most likely to actually push closer than their usual spot given their natural inclination to race prominently.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Brains Controls; Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Brains leads uncontested at a fair pace and the race develops into a test of cruising speed rather than a stamina grind.
scenarios.body: Brains sets a calm fractions through the first half of the race, allowing the two or three horses immediately behind to travel comfortably and strike when the tempo lifts entering the final two furlongs; on Good ground at this trip the runner sitting second or third has a clear positional edge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Drifts; Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Brains sets an overly steady early tempo and the field concertinas, allowing genuine hold-up horses to close the gap entering the straight.
scenarios.body: A very slow early pace compresses the field and removes Brains's advantage, giving the best horses in the race a fair run regardless of position; those with the highest RPR and best recent Good-ground form get the best of this.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Mid-Race Surge; Midfield Types Benefit
scenarios.trigger: If one of the redistributed prominent types pushes forward and injects a sharper middle-sectional pace, fragmenting the field before the home turn.
scenarios.body: A contested or quickening middle portion strings the field out and the runners who travelled best without expending energy fighting for position land in the prime spots turning in; horses with strong Good-ground profiles and a history of winning from just off the pace are best placed.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaotic Pace; Market Movers Late
scenarios.trigger: If the large field causes a bunched start and multiple runners push for position through the early stages, creating a messy tempo.
scenarios.body: Runners caught wide or blocked in the early stages struggle to recover their rhythm on a flat, right-handed track that offers few hiding places; the only beneficiaries are horses with exceptional tactical speed who avoid early traffic and arrive late with a clear run.

watchPoints.text: Brains's early position is everything — if he misses the break or is pushed wide by the 18-runner draw, the entire pace map collapses and the projected controlled pace becomes uncertain; watch the stalls closely.

Glen Breeze and Distillate are natural prominent types squeezed into midfield on the map — if either pushes forward aggressively in the first furlong, they could inject an unplanned mid-race surge and compromise the chances of horses who rely on a steady tempo.

The absence of a declared jockey for Gordon Bennett is a flag; a late change or unknown tactical instruction on an 8-year-old hold-up horse could create unpredictable early movement from a runner near the rear of an already crowded 18-strong field.

Tamazu returns from 361 days off and, regardless of how the pace unfolds, represents a significant fitness question that could cause interference if the horse is ring-rusty in the early stages of a tightly-packed field.

Whatswrongnow stepping up to 7½f from recent 5-6f efforts is worth monitoring in the straight — if stamina gives out approaching the final furlong, a horse sitting just behind could be hampered by a rapidly weakening rival mid-track.

races.name: Lidan Handicap

runners_data.name: Eddie G
runners_data.note: Won twice at 7f on Good ground recently and clearly thrives on this going/trip combination; apprentice Sam Coen (5lb claim) adds value and from a prominent pitch he is well-placed to pounce on any leader who over-controls the tempo.
runners_data.comment: Eddie G has won two of his last five starts, including back-to-back victories, and returns with experience of today's distance and going, but our figures rank him tenth of thirteen and he faces a stiff ask at 140 lb from stall 13.

runners_data.name: Engines On
runners_data.note: Ran just 2 days ago which is a significant fitness and freshness concern; beat at odds-on last time on Good at this trip and while prominent-styled, the very quick turnaround for a six-year-old is the overriding factor to watch.
runners_data.comment: Engines On won five starts back but has been unplaced in his four subsequent runs, and returning just two days after his last outing raises a fitness query; he has run over today's trip and going, though a stall-eight draw and 139 lb are neutral factors to weigh.

runners_data.name: Plume Noire
runners_data.note: Absent 352 days and returning from a long layoff for a trainer with a modest recent strike rate — hold-up style suits a closer's scenario but fitness on this evidence is a serious query.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and absent for 352 days, Plume Noire does arrive with fitness questions, yet she has run over today's distance and going before and a speed rating of 90 gives her strong claims, with our rating of 88 suggesting she is better than her official mark of 79.

runners_data.name: Earls
runners_data.note: Consistent second-placer at 8f on Good and Soft; Gary Carroll's booking adds confidence, but the horse drops to 7½f and holds a prominent style that should see him well positioned — multiple near-misses suggest a win is overdue.
runners_data.comment: Placed second on three consecutive occasions in recent starts, Earls arrives here fit on a 13-day turnaround, with experience of today's trip and going, and our rating of 82 marks him as a leading threat; the risk is that he remains winless in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Tokyo Treasure
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with Good-ground form from every recent run; drops slightly in distance and the 13d break looks fine, but yet to win at this trip and finishing record (0W2P on sim-going) shows consistency without the killer blow.
runners_data.comment: Tokyo Treasure is winless in his last five starts, and ranked last on our figures with a speed rating well below par, making him hard to fancy at the weights; he does at least return on a quick turnaround with experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Goal Exceeded
runners_data.note: Strong in-form hold-up type who won at 7f on Good and finished fourth twice since — Adam Caffrey's claim is small but useful, and this horse's profile is the one that benefits most if midfield closers get a late look in.
runners_data.comment: Ranked well down the field on our figures, Goal Exceeded faces a stiff ask in a 13-runner field, and two starts without a win — fourth and fourth since his latest success — underline the concern; he has run over today's trip and going before, and a recent outing 22 days ago means he comes here fresh enough.

runners_data.name: Gavoo
runners_data.note: Three-year-old who has run consistently well on Good ground at 6f; steps up to 7½f here for the first time and that stamina question is unresolved — a hold-up style means he needs the race to be truly run.
runners_data.comment: Gavoo rates considerably higher than his official mark of 80 suggests, and having run over today's trip and going he arrives with clear conditions experience; third two starts back shows he can hit the frame, though his last six efforts have left him yet to score and that winless run is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Morehampton
runners_data.note: JP Murtagh-trained three-year-old whose hold-up style on Good ground looks genuine; ran third at 7f last time, but form at 6f and mixed finishing positions suggest reliability is not yet confirmed at this trip.
runners_data.comment: Morehampton showed up with a third last time out after a string of disappointing efforts, and he has run over today's distance and going before, but he remains winless in recent starts and a trainer in the depths of a 28-run losing run is a concern heading in.

runners_data.name: Punica Granatum
runners_data.note: The one confirmed pace-setter; Shane Foley is a high-class booking and the horse has led into a place at 8f before — uncontested in front on Good ground, the risk is that a lenient early gallop actually allows him to last home rather than collapse.
runners_data.comment: Placed third last time out and a second four starts back, Punica Granatum arrives here fit on 16 days' rest, carrying 130 lb from stall one, with experience over today's trip and going boosting her claims; the risk is that she remains yet to win in her last five starts.

runners_data.name: Highbury See See
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse whose recent form (3rd, 4th on Good at 8f) shows genuine ability when getting its run; the crowded midfield position it will actually occupy in this race is not its natural territory, tempering its winning chance despite fair form.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and returning after 66 days off, Highbury See See faces a stiff ask, though a third two starts back and a fourth four starts back offer some encouragement, and he has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Merisi Diamond
runners_data.note: Won at 7f on Soft in April but its going sim-rate on Good is 0W0P from three runs — that is the key concern here; prominent style is suitable but going preference makes this a tentative entry in this particular race shape.
runners_data.comment: Merisi Diamond won last time out but that success came 134 days ago, and a seventh and sixth in the two starts before it raise questions about consistency; he has run over today's distance and going, and 128 lb from stall two gives him a workable enough profile, though the fitness query after such a lengthy absence is real.

runners_data.name: Mercurial
runners_data.note: Naturally prominent-running seven-year-old with a decent record at 6f on Good; the busy midfield it will be forced to occupy as a consequence of this field's composition is not where it does its best work, and that position adjustment meaningfully reduces its winning chances.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Mercurial does bring distance and going experience to the table, and a second two starts back hints at residual ability, though an eighth last time out is harder to gloss over; the 127 lb burden won't help his cause from stall five.

runners_data.name: Ninth Crusade
runners_data.note: Colin Keane takes the mount which upgrades interest significantly, but the horse's genuine hold-up profile means it needs a strong pace to close into — mapped toward midfield, it will likely race further back still, making Keane's tactical read pivotal.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 12 of 13 on our figures, Ninth Crusade is hard to fancy, though he does have experience over today's trip and going, and a third last time out offers a crumb of comfort.

races.paceDynamic: Punica Granatum is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 13-runner 7½f Roscommon handicap and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, Shane Foley can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good ground that plays squarely to a prominent or tracking profile. Eddie G, Engines On, Earls, and Tokyo Treasure will all seek to press close to the pace, meaning the early order directly behind the leader will be competitive and physical, with several horses shuffled back from their natural positions. The field contains more prominent-minded types than can realistically secure that ground — Mercurial is a confirmed prominent racer who will be squeezed toward midfield — while Highbury See See and Ninth Crusade, both genuine hold-up horses, are also mapped to midfield but will race from further back than their notation suggests. With one honest pace-setter controlling the race and Good ground ensuring consistent underfoot conditions throughout, this shape heavily favours horses who can sit just off the leader in the first three or four positions and produce a sustained run from two furlongs out — prominent trackers with a turn of foot on Good ground are the profile to beat.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Punica Sets, Trackers Win
scenarios.trigger: If Punica Granatum leads at a fair clip and the prominently-placed horses behind settle and pounce from two out.
scenarios.body: Punica Granatum's uncontested lead creates an honest, even gallop that rewards horses travelling comfortably just behind — those in positions two through four will hit the rising ground fresh and kick on.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Steady Gallop, Leader Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Punica Granatum controls the pace so efficiently that the lead is never truly surrendered and the field is strung out behind.
scenarios.body: A controlled fractions race on Good ground suits a relaxed front-runner and Foley may simply never be headed if the challengers use too much energy jockeying for tracking positions.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Closers Pick Up
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely brisk enough in the first half to stop the prominent horses and the closers from midfield sustain a strong late run.
scenarios.body: Goal Exceeded and Gavoo, holding course form on Good ground, would be the chief beneficiaries of any late collapse of those up with the pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Hold-Ups Land
scenarios.trigger: If the front runners set an unusually fast gallop that burns off the prominent horses and leaves late closers with most ground to make up but most to gain.
scenarios.body: This is structurally unlikely given only one true front-runner, and depends on redistributed hold-up types Ninth Crusade and Highbury See See racing closer to their natural style than the map suggests, which is improbable given the field size.

watchPoints.text: Engines On ran just 2 days ago — monitor its paddock condition and early movement closely, as a six-year-old returning on a 48-hour turnaround on Good ground is a significant physical ask.

Punica Granatum's gallop tempo in the first three furlongs will define the entire race — if Foley steals an uncontested lead at a crawl, horses like Earls and Eddie G tracking close must be sharp enough to respond early rather than wait.

Mercurial and Ninth Crusade are both likely to end up racing out of their most effective positions given the density of prominent and hold-up types in this field — watch how both jockeys (Heffernan, Keane) navigate the first furlong to see if either can claim a more natural berth.

Plume Noire's 352-day absence means its early behaviour in the parade ring and at the start is worth monitoring — a hold-up horse returning cold after nearly a year is vulnerable to blowing its race before the gates open.

Goal Exceeded has won and placed multiple times at this trip on Good ground and is the hold-up runner with the most convincing case for a late run — watch its position entering the final two furlongs as the key timing indicator for the closers' scenario.

races.name: Lecarrow Race

runners_data.name: Hazdann
runners_data.note: D K Weld's 4yo has won on Good ground at 7f and is proven prominent in that style, making the step to 1m2½f the key question; Chris Hayes takes the ride and the 85-day absence is a minor concern, though Weld horses return fit and sim-going record is solid (4/4 on Good).
runners_data.comment: Hazdann boasts a win three starts back on today's going, and as the top-rated runner he holds solid claims despite a seventh last time out and a return from 85 days off.

runners_data.name: God Of Power
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery trains and rides this 3yo, who has winning form at 7f on Good but holds a prominent racing style that cannot be accommodated at the head of this field — likely to find itself further back than it wants, which the 0.92 style-fit flag reflects.
runners_data.comment: God Of Power arrives in solid recent form, third last time out and a winner four starts back, with going experience in his favour and a 24-day gap suggesting he's kept fresh; the main risk is that our rating of 82 leaves him with something to find on the figures.

runners_data.name: Handshake
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's lightly raced 3yo (only two career runs) showed a win at 8f on Standard going and gets the run of the race as the lone front-runner; headgear (hood/tongue-tie flagged) is noted and the step to 1m2½f on Good turf is an unknown, but uncontested lead gives it every chance.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of five on our figures and his speed rating of 56 gives little encouragement, though he does bring a win two starts back and has experience of today's going to his name.

runners_data.name: Dial Me In
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse for O'Brien who has placed at 10f on Good going, but a zero finish last time and a history of mid-pack performances (8th, 13th in recent runs) demands a genuinely honest gallop from Handshake that may not materialise in this small field.
runners_data.comment: Dial Me In arrives here with experience over today's trip and going, and a second three starts back suggests he retains the ability to threaten at this level; the concern is that he has been winless in recent starts and his last two efforts have been well below that earlier form.

runners_data.name: Sinmara
runners_data.note: O'Brien's 3yo won at 8f on Soft and has placed form, but its natural prominent style is squeezed out by the race shape, forcing it into a midfield slot — the 0.93 style-fit flag is a genuine concern and the drop to 128lbs does not fully compensate for the positional disadvantage.
runners_data.comment: Sinmara showed she can win when taking the prize four starts back, and her experience on today's going is a positive at 128 lb from stall four, but she must reverse recent form after finishing sixth and seventh in her last two starts.

races.paceDynamic: Handshake is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with only five runners and no genuine challenger for the lead, is set to bowl along at a controlled, uncontested gallop from the outset. Hazdann will press from a prominent position just off the leader, while God Of Power and Sinmara — both natural prominent types — are pushed back into a midfield role they would not naturally choose, meaning the pace ahead of the closers is not as deep as the headcount of prominent-style runners might suggest. Dial Me In will settle at the rear and will need Handshake to either go hard enough to set up a finishing kick or fade in the straight. This field holds more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate; Hazdann is best placed to secure the position closest to Handshake, with God Of Power and Sinmara likely shuffled further back than ideal. The race shape strongly favours a horse that can travel prominently at a controlled tempo and sustain its effort around the turn into the straight — a profile that suits Hazdann and, to a lesser extent, Handshake itself if it can control fractions and quicken.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Handshake Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Handshake dictates a comfortable, uncontested pace and arrives at the straight with reserves intact.
scenarios.body: Handshake, with no rival willing or able to press it, sets a fractions-controlled tempo that turns the race into a test of class and stamina in the straight; Hazdann, travelling prominently throughout, is ideally placed to challenge but Handshake's class advantage (OR 120) makes it hard to peg back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Handshake's early pace proves just sufficient to drain it and Hazdann sweeps past in the straight.
scenarios.body: Hazdann, settled just off the leader's shoulder throughout, has the fitness to sustain a challenge having won on this going at 7f; the trip extension to 1m2½f on Good ground suits a horse who has already won at 7f on Good.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Finish Into Places
scenarios.trigger: If Handshake cuts a fraction too brisk for a small field and Dial Me In or displaced midfielders get a late run.
scenarios.body: Dial Me In has placed at 10f on Good going and can finish strongly if the pace collapses in the straight, though its recent form (0 in last run) gives concern; God Of Power and Sinmara, racing out of role in midfield, would need a genuine test of stamina to compensate for their unnatural position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Muddled Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Handshake's fractions slow dramatically and the race bunches entering the straight, creating a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: A sprint-like finish over 1m2½f on Good ground would scramble the form, though no horse in this field stands out as a specialist for a truly compressed finish; God Of Power's one-off winning form at 7f on Good is the best match here if pace collapses suddenly.

watchPoints.text: Watch Handshake's early sectionals — if Scott McCullagh allows a completely uncontested crawl, the race may be decided by a sprint in the straight that favours class over pace shape, handing Handshake a near-unassailable advantage.

God Of Power and Sinmara are both natural prominent types who cannot get their preferred position — monitor whether either applies pressure to Handshake in the early stages or accepts a passive midfield role that blunts their chance.

Hazdann's 85-day absence for D K Weld is worth tracking in-running; if the horse travels freely early it suggests fitness is not an issue, but any signs of greenness or fatigue on the turn will matter.

Dial Me In requires a genuine pace in a five-runner field to get competitive — if the race is run at a dawdle from Handshake, Declan McDonogh's hold-up tactics will find the straight too short to make meaningful ground.

races.name: Racing Here Again On September 28th Maiden

runners_data.name: Coolnagrattan
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with solid placed form at 12f on Good; T14 form (0/4) is modest but Seamie Heffernan adds tactical intelligence, and 33 days since last run leaves fitness as a minor query at 4yo mark.

runners_data.name: Nothingbutadream
runners_data.note: Hold-up type flagged for fading in the finish, which is a significant concern at 1m4f from the rear in a slowly-run race; 16 days since last run and Good ground suit on paper but the tactical situation leaves little hope.

runners_data.name: Nugentstown Sue
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare with a 278-day absence and a pattern of fading finishes; best placed run came 5th of 16f and similar-going record is thin, making this a speculative reappearance at age 7 after a long layoff.

runners_data.name: Shemiyka
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who steps up to 1m4f from 10f, a trip she hasn't tried; visor fitted and trainer M D O'Callaghan in decent 14-day form (2/11), so she could improve at the trip if she settles.

runners_data.name: Almazann
runners_data.note: Has placed second in all three career starts on Good at 10-12f for Dermot Weld, making her the most consistent profile in the field; 13 days since last run is fine and the prominent style means she is perfectly placed to make her mark here.

runners_data.name: Daily Wonder
runners_data.note: Completely unexposed debutant for T G McCourt with no going or form data available; lightly raced tag and unknown commodity status make assessment impossible — treat as a pure wildcard.

runners_data.name: Four Ball
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with one run showing a 6th at 12f on Good 80 days ago; the gap since last run is the main concern, though the trip should suit and a fresh mind could help.

runners_data.name: Nemorino
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead debutant with no form or going data; the trainer is in strong 14-day form (6/27) and stable debuts at this trip are always worth noting — style entirely unknown.

runners_data.name: Plug In Hybrid
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Colin Keane and Noel Meade stepping from 9f to 1m4f; only one run on the board (6th on Good) so the trip extension is a question, but the prominent style suits this pace shape well.

runners_data.name: Purple Bandit
runners_data.note: John Harrington debutant ridden by Shane Foley with blinkers flagged; stable in 14-day form (2/28) and Foley's booking on an unexposed type always commands respect — complete unknown but well-connected.

runners_data.name: Cosmetic
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for Aidan O'Brien with best form showing a 2nd at 12f on Good; from a prominent to hold-up position at the rear, she needs a stronger pace than Mawhibah is likely to set — Wayne Lordan is a significant positive.

runners_data.name: I Hope You Dance
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse in form (placed twice at 12f) that has been redistributed to midfield because the rear of this 19-runner field is already packed with hold-up types; the style-fit discount (0.92) is material and Henry De Bromhead's strong yard (6/27) is the best thing working in its favour here.

runners_data.name: Kigalienne
runners_data.note: Second Harrington debutant in the race alongside Purple Bandit; Scott McCullagh takes the ride and the stable's two-pronged approach suggests at least one may be well-prepared, but no evidence to separate them.

runners_data.name: Mawhibah
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner for Joseph Patrick O'Brien's in-form yard (T14: 12/71); has raced prominently and her recent 2nd at 12f on Good suggests she handles the trip — the key question is whether her class matches the licence to dictate.

runners_data.name: Miss Romagna
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a 2nd and 3rd in Good-ground runs, giving her the most relevant placed form profile outside Almazann; 51 days since last run is the only mild concern and W J Lee is a reliable booking.

runners_data.name: Shambata
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for J P Murtagh that showed little in two runs at 10f on Good; the step to 1m4f could suit in theory but the race shape offers hold-up horses almost no assistance today.

runners_data.name: Metallic
runners_data.note: Hold-up type flagged for fading, trained by Joseph Patrick O'Brien who already has Mawhibah as the stable's pace weapon; a single run of 8th at 12f on Good offers minimal encouragement — no jockey listed is also a note.

runners_data.name: Gentle Soda
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner that fades in the finish, with a single 12th of 8 on Good for E McNamara; every data point here points away from this race shape and the fade flag compounds the concern.

runners_data.name: Michinaga
runners_data.note: Lightly raced unknown for Charles Weld with two modest runs (6th, 9th) at shorter trips; the step to 1m4f is speculative but Weld's patient approach with this type can yield improvement — worth monitoring market.

races.paceDynamic: Mawhibah is the lone confirmed front-runner in a 19-runner maiden over 1m4f at Roscommon, and with no other genuine pace challenger likely to press her from the front, she is set to control this race at a measured, sustainable gallop on Good ground. Coolnagrattan, Almazann, Miss Romagna, Plug In Hybrid, and Shemiyka will look to track close behind in the prominent group, creating a compact early order but no real headlong gallop. The large hold-up contingent — Nothingbutadream, Nugentstown Sue, Cosmetic, Shambata, Metallic, Gentle Soda — will be racing from well off the pace, and with I Hope You Dance redistributed to midfield because the rear of the field is already saturated with hold-up types, true closers will need a strong pace to bring them into play; that pace is unlikely to materialise. This race shape most favours prominent-racing types who can sit a length or two off Mawhibah's controlled fractions and pick up sharply in the straight, rather than horses whose wins depend on a strong tempo dragging them into contention from the back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Mawhibah Controls, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Mawhibah dictates a steady pace unchallenged and the prominent group tracks efficiently before quickening in the straight.
scenarios.body: Mawhibah sets a comfortable tempo, never pressured, and the race becomes a test of quality in the final two furlongs rather than stamina; horses who have tracked within two or three lengths the whole way are ideally placed to strike. Almazann's consistent placed form at this trip on Good and Coolnagrattan's similar-going experience make them the most likely to finish over the top.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Mawhibah's controlled fractions allow her to conserve enough energy to repel challengers in the straight on Good going.
scenarios.body: With no rival forcing a genuine test, Mawhibah's lead is never threatened early and she simply extends her advantage into the final furlong on minimal reserves; Joseph Patrick O'Brien's in-form yard (T14: 12/71) adds significant confidence to the hold-on scenario. Miss Romagna and Coolnagrattan represent the most likely chasing threats.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Unknown Debutants Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If one or more of the lightly raced unknown quantities — Purple Bandit, Nemorino, Kigalienne, or Daily Wonder — possesses undetected class and strikes from an unexposed position.
scenarios.body: Maidens at this trip regularly produce a debut or lightly raced winner who bypasses the tactical battle entirely; Shane Foley on Purple Bandit or Henry De Bromhead's Nemorino represent the most credible unknown threats given connections. Their going assessments are unknown, which adds uncertainty, but unexposed types regularly land big-field maidens.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If an unexpected injection of pace mid-race stretches the field and allows hold-up horses to motor through on the bridle.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely shape given Mawhibah's uncontested lead and the overcrowded hold-up contingent; I Hope You Dance, though a genuine hold-up type, is running out of its natural rear position and the style-fit discount (0.92) meaningfully reduces its chance of delivering in this scenario. Cosmetic, backed by Aidan O'Brien and ridden by Wayne Lordan, is the truest closer to consider if the pace surprisingly heats up.

watchPoints.text: Almazann has placed second in every career start on Good ground and her prominent style puts her perfectly in the slipstream of Mawhibah — if she travels well into the straight, she is the biggest threat to the front runner.

Mawhibah sets the entire tempo of this race unchallenged; if she is allowed a soft lead and finds an extra gear off the home bend, the race could be over before closers from the hold-up group get organised.

Purple Bandit and Nemorino are both debutants from well-regarded yards (Harrington, De Bromhead) with completely unknown profiles — watch early market moves on either, as stable confidence could signal something the data cannot.

The hold-up group (Nothingbutadream, Nugentstown Sue, Gentle Soda, Metallic) is unusually large for this race shape and all are flagged as faders; if Mawhibah sets a slow pace, this entire cohort is likely to be flattering to deceive in the straight.

I Hope You Dance is a true hold-up type racing from a midfield map position due to overcrowding at the rear — its style-fit discount means any prominent finish should be viewed with that context in mind rather than as confirmation of tactical versatility.

races.name: Oran Handicap

runners_data.name: Sea Eagle
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up performer for Gerard O'Leary who needs to come from off the pace, but with 19 runners and a slow pace his finishing run risks getting bottled up; 24 days fresh, goes on good ground, poor recent form string of /600-0 is a concern at this level.
runners_data.comment: Sea Eagle arrives here rated 88 by our assessors — top of a 19-runner field — has run over today's trip and going, and returns on a fresh 24-day break carrying 140 lb; the concern is that he has been winless in his last four starts.

runners_data.name: Superficial
runners_data.note: Andrew McNamara's charge has respectable good-ground form (1W1P in similar going) and a decent form string of 3-2610, but a 30-day absence and a deep hold-up style means this moderate tempo over 1m4f may not generate enough pace to suit; Gavin Ryan on board is a positive.
runners_data.comment: Superficial won two starts back but has been unplaced on his most recent outing, and 140 lb is no small ask; he has run over today's trip and going before, and a rating of 84 offers some encouragement, though he must bounce back here.

runners_data.name: Thyer
runners_data.note: Leigh Roche partners this consistent hold-up type who has placed at 10f and 12f on good ground, and a 15-day turnaround suggests he is fit; while his natural style places him at the back, his OR79 and recent placed efforts make him a live candidate if the pace quickens sufficiently in the straight.
runners_data.comment: Thyer has been knocking on the door, finishing second last time out and third two starts back, yet he remains winless in his last five starts and that lack of a killer blow is the concern; experience over today's trip and going counts in his favour, and he arrives here on a quick turnaround of 15 days looking fit enough.

runners_data.name: Fratas
runners_data.note: Joseph Patrick O'Brien's 6-year-old is a hold-up performer on a downward form trajectory (244-60) and the most recent run was a distant 10th at 12f on good ground; 30 days between runs and no win on good ground in this form cycle make it hard to get enthusiastic.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Fratas does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and her rating of 84 suggests she retains ability, though an unplaced effort last time and 138 lb to carry are the chief concerns.

runners_data.name: Neptunes Staircase
runners_data.note: Colin Keane takes the mount for G M Lyons and this is a key booking — a prominent-style horse who should sit just off Stellar Moment, and a 156-day absence since a good 1f win at 12f gives him a freshness angle; the layoff is the only query in what looks an ideal tactical position.
runners_data.comment: Neptunes Staircase showed he retains winning ability with a victory two starts back, and has run over today's trip and going, with our rating of 87 marking him out as a serious threat in a wide field; the chief concern is that ninth last time out and 156 days off the track.

runners_data.name: Royal Saxo
runners_data.note: A prominent racer for A J Martin wearing a hood (hg:t), but recent form reads 2-9957 and he has failed to place at 12-13f on good ground in his latest runs; Robbie Colgan takes over but the form collapse is difficult to overlook even from a handy berth.
runners_data.comment: Royal Saxo has been struggling for form in his last four starts but does boast a second five starts back, and he has run over today's trip and going before, returning after 30 days off carrying 138 lb, yet to score in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Merlin The Wizard
runners_data.note: R P Cody's 6-year-old wears a hood (hg:p), has won twice over 10-12f on good ground, and is 16 days fresh; a genuine hold-up type who is capable if the race develops into a strong-pace finish, though a benign tempo set by Stellar Moment works against him getting a proper tow into the race.
runners_data.comment: Merlin The Wizard won twice in his last six starts, two starts back showing a sixth and carrying 136 lb here after just 16 days, though consecutive below-par efforts at the end of that sequence give pause, even if he has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Zoffman
runners_data.note: Noel Meade's veteran (OR74) is a true hold-up performer pushed into the midfield map — the crowded field makes it almost impossible for him to find his natural rearward position; recent form (0-6803) is moderate and the STYLE_FIT of 0.90 tempers expectations, even though he handles good ground.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Zoffman nonetheless catches the eye on a rating of 86 — well clear of his official mark — and returns in good time on 16 days' rest, having run over today's trip and going before; the risk is that elusive recent form.

runners_data.name: Faro Island
runners_data.note: Gary Carroll rides this lightly-raced 4-year-old who has two wins over 10-12f on good and soft and a promising form figure of -41761; though mapped to midfield from a true hold-up position, Carroll's race-reading ability could help him find a forward enough berth to capitalise — one of the more interesting profiles despite the redistribution caveat.
runners_data.comment: Faro Island won last time out and has experience of today's trip and going, but ranked sixteenth of nineteen on our figures he faces a stiff ask, and the two wins in his last five starts are sandwiched around a pair of poor efforts that make him difficult to trust.

runners_data.name: Flying Fortress
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's 4-year-old returns after 62 days and has placed twice over 10f on good ground; a natural hold-up horse relocated into midfield on the map, and the STYLE_FIT of 0.94 means the positional compromise is relatively minor, but the extended break and recent 0-5082 form cloud his prospects.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and drawn from a midfield berth on a 62-day absence, Flying Fortress at least has experience of today's distance and going to call upon, and a rating of 78 offers a slim edge over his official mark of 73, though the weight of 133 lb is no help.

runners_data.name: Youcansaythatagain
runners_data.note: W J Lee rides this lightly-raced 3-year-old for A Oliver — only three career runs but a win over 10f on good ground last time; naturally prominent-racing, which is ideal for this shape, and a low OR of 82 with age allowance means the handicapper may not have fully caught up with his ability yet.
runners_data.comment: Won two starts back but beaten into fifth last time out, Youcansaythatagain has going experience to call on and returns on a quick turnaround of 15 days; his official mark of 82 suggests he has ability, though he may need to find more from that latest disappointing effort.

runners_data.name: Letiza
runners_data.note: Trainer-rider Andrew Slattery partners his own horse, who is only 9 days since his last run and carries a form line of 60-244; a genuine hold-up type redistributed to midfield, the quick back-up suggests fitness but the benign pace and crowded mid-division look unhelpful for his natural finishing style.
runners_data.comment: Letiza arrives here in good shape on a nine-day turnaround, and her second three starts back offers encouragement, yet she has been winless in her last five starts and a 132 lb burden may prove testing against stronger rivals.

runners_data.name: Stellar Moment
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner in the race for John O'Donoghue, ridden by claimer Rory Mulligan (5lb); won last time at 12f on soft and has placed at 12f on good, and with no genuine pace rival to challenge him she should control every fraction — the apprentice claim is the lone tactical risk if the field swarms her in the straight.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 17 of 19 on our figures, Stellar Moment faces a stiff ask, and a career-high 129 lb adds to the challenge; but she arrives a winner last time out, has run over today's trip and going, and returns on a fresh 31-day break.

runners_data.name: Adel
runners_data.note: M D O'Callaghan's 3-year-old returns after 62 days with a win at 12f on good ground buried in a patchy form string (7-8710); a hold-up runner who needs the race to develop strongly in the straight, and the extended layoff adds uncertainty despite the course-appropriate trip.
runners_data.comment: Adel won two starts back but has been unplaced on his most recent outing, and 62 days off the track raises a fitness query; he has run over today's distance and going, and his rating of 80 gives him a slim edge over his mark.

runners_data.name: Lord Aus
runners_data.note: Ben Coen — a top booking — rides J P Murtagh's 3-year-old who has placed three times over 10-13f on good ground and won at 12f; a true hold-up type that the map places in midfield, but Coen's positional intelligence means he could manufacture a forward enough position to be dangerous in the straight, making him one of the more compelling hold-up prospects.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out and a winner two starts back, Lord Aus shows some recent consistency, but ranked 18 of 19 on our figures and saddled by a trainer without a winner in 28 attempts over the past fortnight, he is extremely hard to fancy here.

runners_data.name: Ryefield Dasher
runners_data.note: Thomas Gibney's 3-year-old has struggled over 12f on good ground and owns no wins or places at this class on good going; a hold-up horse relocated to midfield with a STYLE_FIT of 0.90, and the moderate form line (45-605) gives little reason to expect improvement in a competitive 19-runner handicap.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Ryefield Dasher is hard to fancy, though he has run over today's trip and going before and returns after a 35-day break with some freshness in his favour.

runners_data.name: Summer Snow
runners_data.note: Peter Lawlor's 6-year-old has three wins on good ground but recent form (905083) and a tongue tie (hg:t) tell a story of inconsistency; 13 days since last run, naturally a hold-up type pushed into midfield, and the benign pace Stellar Moment will set is the wrong environment for a horse needing a proper gallop to close into.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Summer Snow faces a stiff task from 14th in the rankings, and 129 lb is a hefty burden; that said, she returns on a quick turnaround showing some freshness, and does have experience of today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Duke Of Leggagh
runners_data.note: Michael Mulvany's veteran wears a tongue tie (hg:t) and has finished 16th and 16th at 12-16f on good ground in recent starts — catastrophic form; 13 days back and a hold-up style placed in midfield, there is nothing in the numbers to suggest a reversal here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Duke Of Leggagh at least has experience of today's distance and going, and 13 days since his last outing suggests he is fresh; however, his recent run of unplaced efforts makes it hard to fancy him strongly from ninth in the rankings.

runners_data.name: L'Un Deux Trois
runners_data.note: Oliver McKiernan's 10-year-old wears a tongue tie and bit (hg:tb) and has a sim-going record of 13/15 — barely competitive on good ground; a hold-up type on the outer edge of viability at OR66, and the form line (204/01) masks how far back those placed efforts were in large fields at lesser distances.
runners_data.comment: Ranked below the principals on our figures, L'Un Deux Trois makes the running difficult to advocate despite winning last time out — that sole victory in his last five starts is sandwiched around some disappointing efforts, and he sits 15th of 19 on our ratings here.

races.paceDynamic: Stellar Moment is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 19-horse field and, crucially, faces no meaningful pace pressure from any rival capable of matching her to the lead — Neptunes Staircase and Youcansaythatagain are the only two genuine prominent types, meaning Stellar Moment should dictate a controlled, unchallenged gallop from the outset over this 1m4f trip on good ground. With no horse willing or able to collar her early, the pace is likely to be honest rather than scorching, producing a steady-to-moderate tempo that compresses the field behind her and dramatically reduces the advantage of coming from off the pace. This race shape — one leader, two chasers, and a mass of hold-up horses — classically rewards those who can sit close enough in the first half-dozen lengths to pounce in the straight rather than those making up significant ground from the rear. The field is severely overloaded with hold-up types: Lord Aus, Zoffman, Flying Fortress, Faro Island, Letiza, Ryefield Dasher, Summer Snow, Duke Of Leggagh and L'Un Deux Trois cannot all find their natural position at the rear and several will inevitably be pushed into midfield out of role; of these, Lord Aus and Faro Island are most likely to secure a forward berth than their redistribution implies. This race shape firmly favours the prominent racing profile — horses positioned two to five lengths off Stellar Moment's uncontested lead will be ideally placed to strike when she comes back to them in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Stellar Moment Leads Wire-To-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Stellar Moment bowls along at a moderate, controlled tempo and no rival has the pace or inclination to seriously pressurise her at any stage.
scenarios.body: Unchallenged on the front end, she dictates every fraction, conserves energy through the middle portion of the race, and the strong stayers trying to close from midfield simply run out of real estate on a tight finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just brisk enough that Stellar Moment flattens out in the final two furlongs, enabling a sitting prominent horse to pick her off.
scenarios.body: Neptunes Staircase or Youcansaythatagain, travelling close to the pace without excess effort, inherit the lead inside the final furlong and prove too strong for backmarkers unable to generate a sustained run.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Flyer Weaves Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough that the front two or three tie each other up and the final furlong becomes a true stamina test that benefits a fresh closer.
scenarios.body: A horse that managed to find genuine cover near midfield — most likely Lord Aus or Faro Island, who despite redistribution may secure a position with enough daylight — threads through the weakening leaders.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Scrambles The Result
scenarios.trigger: If the large 19-runner field produces crowding, traffic problems or a pace collapse that reshuffles positions unpredictably in the straight.
scenarios.body: With so many hold-up horses forced out of their natural role and jostling for position, a horse that flukes a clean passage — such as Merlin The Wizard or Thyer — could benefit from others being baulked or forced wide.

watchPoints.text: Stellar Moment sets all the fractions unchallenged — watch whether Rory Mulligan (5lb claimer) adopts a truly patient front-running rhythm or over-quickens early in a 19-runner field, as the entire race shape hinges on the pace she supplies.

Neptunes Staircase is 156 days absent and Colin Keane must place him immediately behind the leader — if the big field crowds Keane out in the early stages and Neptunes Staircase loses his prominent position, his chance is materially damaged.

Lord Aus and Faro Island are listed as redistributed hold-up types but Ben Coen and Gary Carroll respectively are capable of manufacturing a forward berth — watch their positions at the first bend, as either stealing a prominent spot transforms their winning chance significantly.

With 19 runners, the mid-race bunching between the 6f and 10f marks could cause significant crowding for the cluster of hold-up horses forced into midfield out of role — Zoffman, Flying Fortress and Letiza are all vulnerable to being trapped on the inner with no room when the pace inevitably quickens.

runners_data.name: Glen Echo
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for Gavin Cromwell, who is in solid 14-day form (5/35); six runs on similar Good ground with two placings suggest course/going competency, but the 19-runner field risks traffic issues for a horse that needs a clean late run over this 12f-plus trip.

runners_data.name: Priorstown
runners_data.note: Ben Coen in the saddle for JP Murtagh; hold-up style with limited exposure at this 14f trip, stepping up from shorter distances where form has been modest — only one run on comparable Good ground from four attempts, and the step up in trip is unproven.

runners_data.name: Wipeawayyourtears

runners_data.comment: Rated 67 and ranked fourth of nineteen, Sir Trancealot brings distance and going experience and returns from a 49-day break looking to build on a third three starts back, though he remains winless in recent starts and a trainer in the depths of a cold run is the main concern.

runners_data.name: Oh I Do Declare

runners_data.name: Ravens Can Fly

runners_data.name: Canon Law

runners_data.name: Ellens Bay
runners_data.note: Third over 14f on Good last time — the distance is clearly within scope, and the redistribution from true hold-up means she may end up closer to the pace than usual; the fade flag is present but the 1m4f Good record is the most encouraging thing in her file, and trainer Ciaran Murphy is in 14-day form.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts, Ellens Bay does at least return to familiar ground having run over today's going before, and a third last time out offers a crumb of encouragement, though her official mark of 53 and ranking towards the foot of the field make it hard to see her turning things around here.

runners_data.name: Augusta Rock
runners_data.note: Joseph Patrick O'Brien's runner, second over 13f on Good most recently — excellent trip and going profile; redistributed from true hold-up, so may occupy a more forward position than natural, which in a slowly-run race is not necessarily a disadvantage, and the headgear (tb) could sharpen focus.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Augusta Rock at least brings distance and going experience to the table, and that runner-up finish last time out hints at returning form — though 45 days off the track and 134 lb on his back are both factors to weigh against him.

races.paceDynamic: Sir Trancealot is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 19-runner field over 1m4f at Roscommon on Good ground, meaning he is likely to bowl along at a controlled, unhurried tempo with nobody to genuinely pressure him through the early stages. Ravens Can Fly is a prominent-type who may attempt to sit just behind, but with a field this large and only one true pace-setter, the gallop is expected to be steady rather than searching, compressing the field into a bunched convoy through the middle of the race. The race will likely ignite in the straight as those tracking closer to the pace look to quicken, while genuine hold-up horses stuck wide or deep in traffic will face a stiff challenge manufacturing the necessary momentum. This shape strongly favours runners with the tactical speed to travel in the first five or six, as a falsely-run race at this trip on Good ground consistently rewards those who can sit within striking range and kick off a moderate tempo — true closers operating from the back will find the lack of an honest pace insufficient to reel in those dictating up front. Several runners tagged as redistributed — including Premier Princess, Captain Con, Ellens Bay, Augusta Rock, Flagstone Lady, Nosmokewithoutfire, Tintinabulla, Minella Buoy, Princess Rosie, Elzaam Express, and Curious Jane — are genuine hold-up types squeezed into the midfield section of the map because the rear of the field is oversubscribed; of these, Premier Princess and Augusta Rock are most likely to physically secure a position closer to the pace than their natural style suggests.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Stalkers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Sir Trancealot sets a sustainable tempo unchallenged and the race ignites only in the straight.
scenarios.body: Sir Trancealot dictates from the front at a moderate clip, allowing the closest pursuers to travel comfortably and pounce with a decisive turn of foot in the final two furlongs; the lack of genuine pace pressure means those who have been sitting three to five lengths off the lead throughout hold a decisive advantage over deep closers.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Gallops Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Sir Trancealot is left entirely to his own devices and the pace is so uncontested that he steals a march without the field realising.
scenarios.body: With no challenger pushing him early, Sir Trancealot finds a rhythm and simply never comes back to the field, as a disorganised chase from a big field on a flat track fails to coordinate a meaningful challenge; this scenario rewards the bold front-running ride and penalises the fragmented hold-up brigade.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Sweeper Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly falsely run and a horse sitting in fifth to eighth position produces a sustained, well-timed run from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: A slow-motion race bunches the entire field, negating Sir Trancealot's stamina advantage and allowing a fresh, well-positioned midfield runner to quicken past tired leaders as the pace finally lifts; those with good form at this trip on Good ground and a prominent enough position to avoid traffic emerge best.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is surprisingly strong enough to string the field out and genuine hold-up horses find a clear run from the rear.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires the field to fracture more than this single-pace-setter race shape suggests, giving true come-from-behind runners the gaps they need; given nearly all plausible closers here are redistributed hold-up types unlikely to achieve their natural position, this shape is structurally unlikely to reward the deepest-sitting runners.

watchPoints.text: Sir Trancealot is the only confirmed front-runner in a field of 19 — if he is left completely alone by a passive field, monitor whether Seamie Heffernan allows him to dictate an artificially slow early pace that sets up a sprint finish, which could dramatically favour horses within three lengths of him entering the straight.

Canon Law is the only runner to have won over 14f on Good ground in recent form — watch how Rory Cleary positions him in the early stages of a big field, as being caught wide or buried deep in a 19-runner convoy could neutralise what looks like the most directly relevant piece of form in the race.

Wipeawayyourtears has the strongest sim-going record in the field (5/7) and won over 12f on Good — watch whether Gavin Ryan is able to manoeuvre from the hold-up position into a tracking spot by the turn, as the 49-day break and style mismatch with a slow pace are the key risks to monitor.

With at least 10 runners redistributed from their natural hold-up positions, watch for congestion and interference entering the home straight — a 19-runner field at Roscommon over 1m4f with a single pace-setter is structurally susceptible to a chaotic final three furlongs as horses simultaneously try to quicken from mid-pack.
